paragraphs: Visual active search uses visual clues to decide where to look for regions of interest across a large geographic area. Deep reinforcement learning can learn effective search policies, but an end-to-end policy may not fully exploit the labeled information collected during training or search. This becomes particularly important when new search tasks differ from training tasks.

The paper separates the policy into two connected modules. A prediction module uses a representation of the task and the search history to estimate where relevant regions are located. A search module then uses these predictions, together with the history, to decide how to distribute further search effort.

The authors also introduce a meta-learning procedure that trains the combined policy to use supervision available both beforehand and during decisions. Experiments across several problem domains report significant improvements over existing visual active search methods. The contribution is a way to combine learned search behavior with explicit predictions that can benefit from newly acquired information.
neurips-2023-a-partially-supervised-rein.tldr: A modular search policy combines reinforcement learning with supervised predictions to improve visual active search across several tested domains.

paragraphs: Early sensory neurons adapt when the statistics of their inputs change. They adjust the variability of individual responses and reduce correlations between neurons. Together, these operations resemble statistical whitening. The paper asks how a mechanistic model can accomplish this adaptation using both changing synaptic connections and changing neuronal gains.

The proposed model assigns these mechanisms complementary timescales. Synapses change slowly, learning structural properties shared across statistical contexts. Gains change quickly, adapting responses to the current context. The authors derive this division from a whitening objective that separates an inverse whitening matrix into basis vectors associated with synaptic weights and a diagonal component associated with neuronal gains.

Tests on synthetic and natural datasets show that the synapses learn optimal configurations over longer timescales, enabling rapid whitening through gain changes. The result offers a unified computational account of how slow learning can prepare a sensory system for fast adaptation. It establishes this behavior in the proposed model rather than directly demonstrating that biological neurons implement the same objective.
neurips-2023-adaptive-whitening-with-fas.tldr: A sensory adaptation model combines slow synaptic learning with fast gain changes to whiten responses across changing statistical contexts.

paragraphs: Backpropagation provides gradients for continuous computations, which creates difficulties when a model generates discrete latent variables. Training still needs information about how changes to the generating parameters would affect the objective. This paper studies how to approximate that information and gives a mathematical interpretation of a widely used workaround.

The authors show that the Straight-Through heuristic acts as a first-order gradient approximation. They then introduce ReinMax, which incorporates Heun’s method, a second-order numerical method for ordinary differential equations. This connection provides a route to second-order approximation accuracy for the gradients involved in generating discrete variables.

Here, second-order accuracy does not mean computing second derivatives: ReinMax requires neither Hessians nor other second-order derivatives, and the authors describe its computational overhead as negligible. Experiments across multiple tasks report better performance than the compared state-of-the-art methods. The contribution connects a practical training heuristic to numerical approximation and uses that understanding to construct a more accurate alternative with little additional computation.
neurips-2023-bridging-discrete-and-backp.tldr: ReinMax improves gradient approximation for discrete latent variables to second-order accuracy without requiring second derivatives.

paragraphs: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning adapts a pretrained language model by learning a small module while keeping the underlying model fixed. Training on different tasks or domains therefore produces a collection of compact modules with different capabilities. This paper investigates whether those learned modules can become reusable ingredients for further adaptations.

The proposed method combines modules through linear arithmetic on their weights. The authors define addition and negation operations, then compose them into more flexible expressions. Once the original modules have been learned, producing a combined module requires no additional training. The approach therefore operates directly on the stored adaptations.

The paper applies this arithmetic to distribution generalization, multitasking, detoxification, and domain transfer, including detoxification of Alpaca-LoRA. Across the evaluated settings, the resulting modules significantly outperform existing ones. These findings support module arithmetic as a practical way to reuse learned adaptations. The evidence concerns the tested compositions and tasks; it does not establish that every combination of module weights will preserve or combine capabilities successfully.
neurips-2023-composing-parameter-efficie.tldr: Linear arithmetic on lightweight adaptation modules produces useful combined language-model capabilities without additional training.

paragraphs: Wasserstein barycenters describe a form of average between distributions. This paper studies a family with two entropy-related regularization controls, called inner and outer regularization strengths. Different settings connect several previously studied barycenter definitions and also yield additional cases, including a particular form of debiased barycenter.

The authors propose an algorithm built from damped Sinkhorn iterations followed by exact maximization and minimization steps. Their analysis guarantees convergence for any choice of the regularization parameters within the studied formulation. This matters because one computational procedure can cover the different barycenter definitions represented by that family.

They also analyze an inexact version that can use approximate Monte Carlo sampling. For barycenters between discrete point clouds, it provides what the authors identify as the first non-asymptotic convergence guarantees in the free-support, grid-free setting. Such guarantees describe approximation behavior before an unlimited number of iterations. The grid-free setting also means the computation is not restricted to placing the barycenter on a prescribed grid.
neurips-2023-computational-guarantees-fo.tldr: The paper gives convergent algorithms for doubly regularized Wasserstein barycenters, including finite-computation guarantees for a sampling-based, grid-free variant.

paragraphs: Safe reinforcement learning trains agents to pursue rewards while respecting specified constraints. The paper considers a further requirement: a deployed agent should adapt when the allowed constraint thresholds change, without needing to be trained again. It formulates this versatile setting around efficient training and zero-shot adaptation.

The proposed Conditioned Constrained Policy Optimization framework, or CCPO, contains two modules. Versatile Value Estimation approximates value functions under threshold conditions not previously seen. Conditioned Variational Inference incorporates constraint thresholds into policy optimization. Together, these components make the requested constraint level part of how the policy is learned and evaluated.

Experiments show that CCPO improves safety and task performance over the evaluated baselines while retaining data-efficient adaptation to different thresholds without retraining. The findings support policies that can respond to changing requirements rather than being tied to one fixed constraint setting. The reported safety advantage is an experimental result; the abstract does not claim a universal guarantee that every deployed action satisfies every possible threshold.
neurips-2023-constraint-conditioned-poli.tldr: CCPO trains constraint-conditioned policies that adapt to changing safety thresholds without retraining and improve safety and performance in experiments.

paragraphs: Reconstructing viewed images from functional MRI requires extracting visual information from noisy brain measurements. The challenge includes both measurement noise and the complicated way visual content is represented in neural activity. This paper addresses the problem by improving the brain-signal representation before using it to guide image generation.

Training proceeds in two phases. First, a Double-contrastive Mask Auto-encoder pretrains an fMRI feature learner to produce denoised representations. Next, an image auto-encoder guides further tuning so that the learner attends to neural activation patterns that are especially useful for reconstruction. The resulting features condition a latent diffusion model that generates the image.

The authors report high-resolution reconstructions with improved semantic accuracy. On 50-way top-1 semantic classification accuracy, they report a 39.34% improvement over previous state-of-the-art methods. This result concerns how accurately reconstructed images preserve semantic content under that evaluation. The central contribution is the staged preparation of informative fMRI features, connecting noise reduction and visual guidance to the final generative reconstruction.
neurips-2023-contrast-attend-and-diffuse.tldr: A two-stage fMRI feature learner guides latent diffusion to reconstruct high-resolution images with improved semantic accuracy.

paragraphs: Counterfactual fairness asks whether an individual would receive the same outcome in a hypothetical world where they belonged to a different social group. This definition relies on an underlying causal graph, which specifies how sensitive attributes and other features relate. Learning models that meet this criterion can therefore depend on how those causal relationships are handled.

Earlier work established a sufficient route to fairness: exclude features that descend from sensitive attributes in the graph. That rule supports a simple construction, but discards every such descendant feature. Being sufficient does not mean that discarding those features is necessary for every counterfactually fair model.

This paper proposes an algorithm that trains with all available features. The authors provide both theoretical and empirical support that models trained through their method can satisfy counterfactual fairness, addressing the lack of guarantees in earlier approaches that also used all features. The contribution broadens the supported ways to construct fair models while retaining the causal-graph-based meaning of fairness.
neurips-2023-counterfactually-fair-repre.tldr: The paper provides an algorithm with theoretical and empirical support for counterfactually fair learning using all available features.

paragraphs: Optimal stopping concerns deciding when to stop an evolving process. In a non-Markovian setting, relevant information can depend on the history rather than only the current state. Extending neural methods designed for Markovian problems can require substantial expansion of the state and parameter spaces, making the resulting problem difficult to handle.

The paper introduces an optimal stopping policy gradient algorithm, OSPG, that can use recurrent neural networks in this setting. Its key feature is implicit optimization of value functions without recursion. This is intended to mitigate the difficulties that arise when history-dependent problems are forced into recursive value-based formulations.

The algorithm is derived through inference on a new Bayesian-network representation of discrete-time, non-Markovian stopping trajectories. That derivation yields an offline policy gradient procedure and eliminates expensive Monte Carlo policy rollouts. The contribution is therefore both a representation of stopping trajectories and a training method built from it, providing a route for recurrent policies to handle history dependence without the rollout cost described in the abstract.
neurips-2023-deep-recurrent-optimal-stop.tldr: OSPG enables recurrent policies for history-dependent optimal stopping through an offline gradient method that avoids expensive Monte Carlo policy rollouts.

paragraphs: Diffusion models usually learn from examples of the signals they will generate. In inverse problems, those signals may never be directly available: a dataset might contain images while the desired outputs are underlying three-dimensional scenes. The paper studies how to learn a distribution over such hidden signals from indirect measurements.

The approach assumes a known, differentiable forward model that turns an underlying signal into a partial observation. It integrates this model into denoising, linking generation of observable data to generation of the hidden signals. This connection enables end-to-end training of a conditional generative model without directly observing the target signals.

At inference time, the model samples underlying signals consistent with a supplied partial observation. The authors demonstrate the approach on three computer vision tasks, including sampling three-dimensional scenes compatible with a single image. The emphasis on a distribution matters: the method produces possible underlying explanations of an observation, rather than treating the inverse problem as necessarily having one unique answer.
neurips-2023-diffusion-with-forward-mode.tldr: Integrating a known differentiable forward model into diffusion enables learning to generate hidden signals from indirect observations alone.

paragraphs: Physical audiovisual commonsense reasoning aims to infer physical knowledge about objects using both video and sound. The paper identifies two obstacles: existing methods do not fully exploit the different characteristics of multimodal information, and limited causal reasoning makes implicit physical relationships difficult to infer.

Disentangled Counterfactual Learning, or DCL, addresses these issues with two components. A sequential encoder separates video representations into factors that remain stable over time and factors that change. It uses a variational autoencoder with a contrastive objective to maximize mutual information. A counterfactual learning module then models physical relationships among objects under counterfactual interventions.

The combination gives the model distinct representations for persistent and changing information, together with a mechanism for reasoning about altered circumstances. DCL is presented as a plug-and-play module for incorporation into baseline systems. Experiments show improvements to the evaluated baselines and state-of-the-art performance. These results support the usefulness of the proposed representation and counterfactual components for the tested audiovisual reasoning task.
neurips-2023-disentangled-counterfactual.tldr: DCL combines separated static and dynamic video representations with counterfactual learning to improve physical audiovisual reasoning.

paragraphs: Very large language models require hardware that many researchers cannot access locally. This paper investigates whether inference and fine-tuning can instead use devices distributed across the internet. Its motivating observation is that models with more than 50 billion parameters can run efficiently over consumer-grade networks when distributed appropriately.

Two practical problems shape the design: participating devices can disconnect abruptly, and their hardware capabilities vary. The authors develop fault-tolerant inference algorithms and load-balancing protocols that assign model work across devices to maximize total throughput. These mechanisms support a pool of machines whose membership can change during operation.

The resulting decentralized system, Petals, runs Llama 2 with 70 billion parameters and BLOOM with 176 billion parameters. For interactive generation, it achieves speeds up to ten times faster than offloading. Evaluation includes simulations and a real deployment across two continents. The findings support pooling idle resources for large-model access, with the reported speedup tied specifically to the offloading comparison and interactive-generation setting.
neurips-2023-distributed-inference-and-f.tldr: Petals uses fault tolerance and load balancing to run large language models across internet-connected devices, reaching up to tenfold faster interactive generation than offloading.

paragraphs: Data augmentation can improve image classification, particularly when training examples are limited. But combining multiple examples creates a difficulty for differentially private learning, which requires bounding each training image’s contribution to the learned model. This paper investigates why applying methods such as mixup naively performs poorly under those constraints.

The authors introduce two augmentation techniques designed for private training. DP-Mix_Self performs mixup using self-augmented data, adapting the construction of mixed examples to the privacy setting. DP-Mix_Diff incorporates synthetic data generated by a pretrained diffusion model into the mixing process. Both change how augmentation examples are assembled rather than simply applying ordinary multi-sample augmentation unchanged.

DP-Mix_Self achieves state-of-the-art classification performance across the datasets and settings evaluated, and DP-Mix_Diff improves performance further. The findings show that useful augmentation can be designed around the bounded-contribution requirement. The contribution is therefore a pair of privacy-aware mixing methods, together with an investigation of why the straightforward use of existing multi-sample augmentation is ineffective.
neurips-2023-dp-mix-mixup-based-data-aug.tldr: DP-Mix adapts mixup to private learning using self-augmented and diffusion-generated data, improving classification in the evaluated settings.

paragraphs: A decision-making system may need to balance several objectives, with different users valuing them differently. This paper studies how to learn those preferences through comparisons and then compute a nearly optimal policy for an individual user. It assumes a known Markov decision process with a vector-valued reward and an unknown user preference vector.

The authors consider two feedback formats. In the first, the user compares two policies and selects the preferred one. In the second, the user compares two small weighted sets of representative trajectories. The latter changes what the user is asked to inspect while retaining comparisons as the source of preference information.

For both formats, the paper gives an algorithm whose comparison-query requirement scales quasilinearly with the number of objectives. That is close to linear growth, with additional logarithmic factors. The result concerns efficiently obtaining a near-optimal personalized policy within the stated model. Its significance is that the preference-learning burden need not grow explosively as the number of objectives increases.
neurips-2023-eliciting-user-preferences-.tldr: Under a known decision-process model, comparison-based algorithms find nearly optimal personalized policies with query counts growing quasilinearly in the number of objectives.

paragraphs: Time-series forecasting becomes difficult when the patterns governing a sequence change over time. Koopa addresses this non-stationarity using Koopman-inspired representations, which describe complex dynamics through linear operators in a learned embedding. Its architecture separates persistent behavior from behavior that varies with the local temporal context.

A Fourier filter divides the series into time-invariant and time-varying components, and separate Koopman predictors advance their dynamics. Stackable blocks learn hierarchical structure. For changing dynamics, Koopa computes context-aware operators from nearby time points. It can also use incoming ground-truth observations to extend the forecast horizon.

The predictors are integrated into a residual architecture that allows direct optimization of the forecasting objective without the binding reconstruction loss used by earlier Koopman forecasters. Compared with the stated state-of-the-art model, Koopa delivers competitive forecasting performance while saving 77.3% of training time and 76.0% of memory. These results highlight computational efficiency alongside predictive performance, with the savings belonging to the reported comparison.
neurips-2023-koopa-learning-non-stationa.tldr: Koopa separates stable and changing time-series dynamics into Koopman predictors, achieving competitive forecasts with substantial reported training-time and memory savings.

paragraphs: Real-world point clouds often show only part of an object because of limited viewpoints, occlusion, or low resolution. Completion methods trained on predefined object collections can struggle when the scanned object is absent from those collections or poorly represented. This paper explores a different source of guidance for filling in the missing surface.

SDS-Complete uses a pretrained text-to-image diffusion model together with textual semantic information about the incomplete object. It optimizes a complete surface representation at test time. The approach draws on an existing image-generation model without requiring an expensive collection of three-dimensional information for the completion task.

The authors evaluate the method on incomplete scans acquired using real-world depth sensors and LiDAR. They demonstrate effectiveness on objects typically missing from common datasets. The result supports transferring semantic knowledge from text-guided image generation into surface completion. Test-time optimization is central to this approach: completion is obtained by optimizing for the supplied object, rather than relying only on a predefined collection of familiar three-dimensional shapes.
neurips-2023-point-cloud-completion-with.tldr: SDS-Complete uses text semantics and a pretrained image diffusion model to complete partial point clouds, including objects poorly covered by common datasets.

paragraphs: POMP is a method for pretraining prompts used with vision-language models. The goal is to place semantic information covering a broad range of visual concepts into a transferable learned prompt. The paper emphasizes memory and computation efficiency as what makes training with more than twenty thousand classes feasible.

After pretraining, the prompt can be inserted directly into different visual recognition tasks. The authors consider image classification, semantic segmentation, and object detection, reporting improved performance in a zero-shot manner. The same pretrained prompt is therefore intended to carry useful information across multiple forms of visual recognition.

Empirical evaluation reports state-of-the-art performance across 21 datasets. Examples include 67.0% average accuracy on ten classification datasets, reported as 3.1% above CoOp, and 84.4 hIoU on open-vocabulary Pascal VOC segmentation, 6.9 above ZSSeg. These findings support broad prompt pretraining as a reusable source of recognition improvements. The contribution combines coverage of many concepts with demonstrated transfer across tasks, rather than reporting gains for only one recognition setting.
neurips-2023-prompt-pre-training-with-tw.tldr: POMP efficiently pretrains prompts on over twenty thousand classes and transfers them to improve several visual recognition tasks without task-specific training.

paragraphs: Protein design often combines a generator of plausible sequences with a model that guides the search toward desirable properties. This paper introduces diffusioN Optimized Sampling, or NOS, to guide discrete diffusion directly in sequence space. It follows gradients through hidden states of the denoising network.

Working directly with sequences avoids the structure-generation and inverse-folding route discussed in the abstract, including its scarce-data and inverse-design challenges. The authors also use NOS to extend LaMBO, a Bayesian optimization procedure supporting multiple objectives and edit constraints. The resulting LaMBO-2 uses saliency maps to strengthen performance when only limited sequence edits are allowed.

The application targets antibodies with improved expression yield and binding affinity to several therapeutic targets, while imposing locality and developability constraints. Exploratory in vitro experiments achieve a 99% expression rate and a 40% binding rate. These are outcomes of the reported exploratory design effort. They support guided discrete diffusion as a practical sequence-design approach without establishing a universal success rate for other proteins or targets.
neurips-2023-protein-design-with-guided-.tldr: NOS guides discrete diffusion directly over protein sequences, enabling constrained antibody design with promising exploratory laboratory results.

paragraphs: Acquiring high-resolution diffusion MRI data requires long scanning times. This paper addresses angular super-resolution by designing a neural operation around the geometry of diffusion MRI. The objective is to improve angular detail through a model that makes explicit use of the structure of this imaging domain.

The authors extend parametric continuous convolution with Fourier feature mapping, global coordinates, and domain-specific context. These additions form the basis of a fully parametric continuous convolution network, PCCNN. The design brings information about spatial and angular organization into the convolution framework used to process the measurements.

Compared with existing models, PCCNN achieves competitive performance while using significantly fewer parameters. The authors also examine whether the formulation remains useful for downstream analyses, reporting good generalization to fixel-based analysis and neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging. Those evaluations matter because a reconstruction method must support subsequent analysis as well as the super-resolution task itself. The findings therefore connect parameter efficiency with utility in the clinically relevant analyses named in the abstract.
neurips-2023-spatio-angular-convolutions.tldr: A geometry-aware continuous convolution network performs diffusion MRI angular super-resolution competitively with fewer parameters and supports relevant downstream analyses.

paragraphs: Batch normalization is commonly placed before an activation function. This paper finds that reversing the order substantially improves performance for bounded activations such as Tanh across several benchmarks and architectures. The same ordering change generally makes much less difference for ReLU or similar functions.

To investigate, the authors examine output distributions of individual activation functions. Many show asymmetric saturation, meaning their outputs concentrate unevenly toward the bounded extremes. Experiments that deliberately vary this asymmetry support the hypothesis that it helps performance. Normalization after activation also moves asymmetrically saturated outputs near zero, enabling high sparsity and further improvements.

Experiments with Tanh, LeCun Tanh, and Softsign associate the reversed ordering with both improved performance and strong asymmetric saturation. The authors then test a shifted Tanh designed to maintain consistent asymmetry, which achieves higher accuracy than ordinary Tanh in the reversed arrangement. Together, these findings provide experimental support for asymmetry as a useful design property, rather than showing that normalization order has the same effect for every activation.
neurips-2023-tanh-works-better-with-asym.tldr: Experiments link improved performance from placing batch normalization after bounded activations to asymmetric saturation, motivating an even better shifted Tanh.

paragraphs: Monte Carlo policy evaluation estimates a policy’s return using simulated trajectories. With a fixed interaction budget, a common choice is to collect trajectories of equal length. This paper asks whether that schedule uses the budget effectively, measuring quality through the variance of an unbiased return estimator that permits different trajectory lengths.

The authors derive a closed-form variance expression that exposes the suboptimality of fixed-length scheduling under their criterion. It also motivates spending more samples at time steps where additional information would most improve precision. Their algorithm, RIDO, divides the interaction budget into mini-batches and updates the trajectory schedule round by round.

At each round, RIDO chooses a schedule to minimize an empirical, robust estimate of the return estimator’s variance. The paper discusses theoretical properties and evaluates the method across several domains. Results show that RIDO can redirect sampling toward time steps needing greater attention and improve final estimation quality. The contribution concerns allocating evaluation data effectively, with unbiasedness and variance providing the central statistical criteria.
neurips-2023-truncating-trajectories-in-.tldr: RIDO adaptively varies simulation trajectory lengths to spend a fixed interaction budget where it can reduce policy-return estimation variance.

paragraphs: Recommendation unlearning concerns removing the influence of data from recommendation models. The paper starts from RecEraser, which the authors describe as already providing full unlearning completeness. Their goal is to improve model utility and unlearning efficiency by examining how its ensemble of sub-models is organized and combined.

The analysis identifies three potential sources of loss: redundancy, relevance, and combination. UltraRE addresses redundancy by introducing transport weights into clustering to balance collaboration and group balance while improving efficiency. It addresses relevance by ensuring that each sub-model converges on the data assigned to its group.

For combination loss, the method simplifies the estimator that brings sub-model outputs together without sacrificing its efficacy. These changes turn the three-part analysis into a redesigned recommendation-unlearning framework. Experiments on three real-world datasets demonstrate its effectiveness. The contribution is a targeted improvement to an existing complete-unlearning approach, linking clustering, sub-model training, and output combination to the practical goals of recommendation quality and efficient removal.
neurips-2023-ultrare-enhancing-receraser.tldr: UltraRE improves recommendation unlearning by redesigning RecEraser’s clustering, sub-model training, and ensemble combination using a three-part loss analysis.

paragraphs: Research on criminal-justice decision-support tools faces questions about both usefulness and fairness. The paper argues that reliance on a few small datasets makes it difficult to study many real-world aspects of those questions. Its contribution is WCLD, a curated collection of 1.5 million criminal cases from Wisconsin circuit courts.

The dataset draws on public records from 1970 through 2020 and includes constructed attributes such as prior criminal counts and recidivism outcomes. It contains substantial samples from five racial groups, alongside sex and age information. Other fields describe offenses, charge severity, decisions, sentence lengths, filing years, and census-derived neighborhood characteristics.

Pseudo-identifiers for judges, counties, and zip codes provide additional contextual information. The paper also documents dataset construction and supplies a datasheet. This combination of scale, case detail, and contextual attributes is intended to support more rigorous fairness research and investigation of systemic issues. The contribution is research infrastructure for examining those relationships, rather than a finding that any particular decision-support model is fair or effective.
neurips-2023-wcld-curated-large-dataset-.tldr: WCLD provides 1.5 million Wisconsin criminal-case records with demographic, case, and contextual attributes for studying algorithmic fairness and systemic issues.

paragraphs: In the Pandora’s Box problem studied here, each box has an opening cost and a hidden value. Paying the cost reveals that value. The decision-maker must choose which boxes to open and which revealed value to select, aiming to minimize the selected value plus the total cost of opening boxes.

The paper considers correlated values, where information revealed by one box can be related to values in others. Weitzman’s rule is optimal in the independent case. The authors show that the rule also applies directly to the correlated setting, obtaining substantially improved approximation guarantees over earlier work through a simpler algorithm.

This does not make the independent-case optimality claim an optimality claim for arbitrary correlations: the stated correlated-case result is an approximation guarantee. The paper also shows how to implement the rule using only samples from the joint distribution of values. A number of samples polynomial in the number of boxes is sufficient, connecting the theoretical rule to a setting where the distribution is accessed through observations.
neurips-2023-weitzman-s-rule-for-pandora.tldr: Weitzman’s rule extends to correlated Pandora’s Box values with improved approximation guarantees and an implementation requiring polynomially many samples.

paragraphs: Long-range forecasting requires recognizing several kinds of temporal structure at once: local and global correlations, plus repetitions over short and long intervals. WITRAN combines mechanisms for these patterns with a recurrent acceleration method. The goal is to improve forecasting while keeping computation and memory demands manageable.

Its Water-wave Information Transmission framework moves information at two granularities to capture repetitive patterns at different timescales. A Horizontal Vertical Gated Selective Unit recursively selects and combines information to model local and global relationships. A separate Recurrent Acceleration Network reduces the stated time complexity to O(√L) while retaining O(L) memory complexity.

Across four benchmark datasets, the authors report improvements over state-of-the-art methods of 5.80% for long-range forecasting and 14.28% for ultra-long-range forecasting. These findings support the combined architecture in the evaluated settings. The contribution connects richer temporal modeling with computational acceleration, addressing the cost of processing long sequences alongside the problem of identifying which recurring and correlated information is useful for prediction.
neurips-2023-witran-water-wave-informati.tldr: WITRAN combines temporal pattern modeling at two granularities with recurrent acceleration to improve long-range and ultra-long-range forecasting.
